{"analysis":"DeepAgents, built on LangGraph, offers explicit graph-state control (nodes, edges, durable state, check-pointing) which aligns with per-node model selection in a task DAG; this is a strong fit for the router's research goal but adds framework coupling and operational complexity. LangGraph's durability supports critical-path latency measurement and recovery, yet its abstraction may obscure cost attribution per node. Pydantic AI provides typed tool definitions and structured outputs, beneficial for strict schema validation in agent tool calls, but it is less suited to orchestrating multi-node DAGs and lacks built-in checkpointing; using it would require additional state management. DSH is reserved for the outer validation environment, so it is not a candidate for the inner agent platform; this separation clarifies that platform comparison should exclude DSH from runtime selection, though DSH can serve as the benchmark harness. The benchmark reports quality, cost, and critical-path latency, so any platform must support fine-grained per-node metrics; LangGraph's node-level hooks enable this, while Pydantic AI's simpler model may require custom instrumentation. Tradeoffs: LangGraph offers control and observability at the cost of learning curve and boilerplate; Pydantic AI offers type safety and simplicity but lacks orchestration primitives. The scoring rubric weights requirement coverage, evidence accuracy, analysis depth, structure, and HTML validity, implying the final report must cite sources precisely and present tradeoffs clearly. Given the router's focus on per-node selection, LangGraph is the more appropriate foundation, with Pydantic AI as a complementary tool for typed interfaces rather than a full platform. The static task decomposition boundary (application layer) means the platform must not enforce decomposition logic; LangGraph's explicit graph definition fits this boundary well. Overall, the tradeoff favors LangGraph for orchestration and observability, accepting higher complexity, while Pydantic AI is a secondary option for schema-heavy subcomponents."}
